title: Best Sumsub Alternatives for KYC and KYB (2026)
summary: The best Sumsub alternatives for KYC and KYB in 2026: when teams look beyond Sumsub, what to look for instead, and how the leading platforms compare.
body_markdown:
## Why Teams Look Beyond Sumsub


Sumsub packages KYC, KYB and AML screening into configurable flows with a single dashboard, and it has earned its place, especially with crypto platforms onboarding individual traders and small entities across many countries. For a lot of teams it is the right tool. Evaluations usually start for one of four reasons.


**KYB has become the main event.** A platform that onboarded consumers now onboards businesses, and business verification is a different problem: registries, ownership structures, the people behind each entity. Teams want a platform built around KYB rather than one that added it.


**Documents are no longer enough.** Generative AI can manufacture a convincing business or identity end to end. Teams want verification anchored on primary sources, where a registry record either exists or it does not, with cross-signal analysis on top.


**The lifecycle matters more than the flow.** Onboarding is one stage. Risk scoring, review, and continuous monitoring are the others, and teams want all five in one system with one audit trail.


**The business is leaving its first vertical.** Positioning built for one segment does not always travel. A company expanding from crypto into payments, lending or marketplaces often re-evaluates the whole stack.


## What to Look For in a Sumsub Alternative


1. **Registry-first verification.** Direct government registry connections where they exist, and composition from multiple data sources where they do not.
2. **KYB depth, not just KYB presence.** Ownership construction across layers and jurisdictions, including the control prong in the US.
3. **Full-lifecycle coverage.** Collection, verification, risk scoring, review and monitoring in one platform. Our[full-lifecycle KYB piece](https://www.aiprise.com/blog/full-lifecycle-kyb) explains why the gaps between systems are where teams get hurt.
4. **Explainable automation.** AI that does the first pass and writes down its reasoning, so analysts review decisions instead of re-doing them.
5. **Coverage with depth.** Not a map of countries, but working verification in the markets you actually operate in.

### 1. AiPrise


AiPrise is the AI-powered global compliance platform: KYB, KYC, AML screening and AI agents in a single API and dashboard, covering 200+ countries with 100+ data sources and 800+ business data points per entity. Three things make it the strongest alternative for teams whose evaluation started with one of the four reasons above.


**KYB is the architecture, not an add-on.** Verification runs registry-first, ownership is constructed across layers and jurisdictions, and every identified individual gets KYC. The output is a verified ownership picture with sources attached.


**AI agents do the first pass, with reasoning.** Documents, websites and screening hits are reviewed by purpose-built agents, and every decision carries written reasoning a reviewer confirms in seconds and a regulator can read. Customers automate up to 80% of verification workflows.


**The lifecycle is one system.** Collection through continuous monitoring, one record, one audit trail. Conduit cut business onboarding from 3 weeks to 72 hours with AiPrise, and BlindPay cut user verification from 8 minutes to 20 seconds.


### 2. Persona


Persona offers composable identity infrastructure with strong developer ergonomics, letting teams design exactly how a flow behaves. The consideration: configurable means configured by you. Registry routing, KYB depth and the later lifecycle stages are yours to build and validate.


### 3. Trulioo


Trulioo aggregates identity and business data across one of the broadest footprints in the industry. The consideration: it is a data layer, so workflow, decisioning and monitoring are built and maintained by your team.


### 4. Veriff


Veriff is strong at the identity half: document and biometric verification with good fraud detection on the person. The consideration: business verification is thin, so it typically pairs with a separate KYB layer.


### 5. Alloy


Alloy orchestrates identity and risk decisions across data vendors you contract with separately, and is well established with US banks and fintechs. The consideration: it coordinates the stack rather than containing it, and total cost includes the underlying vendors.


## When Sumsub Is Still the Right Choice


If your onboarding is mostly individuals, your footprint is broad rather than deep, and you value configurable flows in a single dashboard, Sumsub does that job well. The evaluation is worth running when the center of gravity has moved to businesses, primary-source verification, or the lifecycle after onboarding.


## How to Run the Evaluation


Bring three real cases: a business with layered cross-border ownership, a thin-file sole proprietor, and an applicant that passed your current checks but turned out to be manufactured. Measure how much of each was verified against a primary source, how much manual work remained, and what the audit trail looks like at the end.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is Sumsub a KYB platform or a KYC platform?


Both, with KYC as the historical center of gravity. Teams whose main job is business verification should test KYB depth specifically.


### Can we migrate without re-verifying our whole base?


Most teams migrate new onboarding first and bring the existing base under continuous monitoring on the new platform, re-verifying on risk triggers rather than all at once.


### What is the biggest difference between the alternatives?


Whether the platform contains the lifecycle or only part of it. Data layers, identity checkers and orchestrators each cover a slice; a full-lifecycle platform covers all five stages.
